## Walkthrough

Adds CI benchmark jobs and local benchmark scripts plus a comparator; changes Gas from signed i64 to unsigned u64 and consolidates GasCounter into a single class; updates VM gas fields and related API signatures to use the new Gas type; replaces some bounds-checked instruction/page accesses with unchecked calls and adds a fast-path and explicit jump handling in the interpreter; removes lazy page initialization and eager allocation flag, introduces a fixed-size PageCache and always-allocate path in Arena; adds a reusable EXTENDED_BUF for program decoding; and small test, lint, and .gitignore adjustments.

## Possibly related PRs

- tomusdrw/anan-as#178: Also modifies gas types and the Gas/GasCounter implementation and updates VM gas-related initializations and usages.  
- tomusdrw/anan-as#83: Adjusts GasCounter subtraction/underflow semantics (clamp-to-zero behavior), overlapping the consolidated GasCounter behavior changes.  
- tomusdrw/anan-as#160: Changes PVM lifecycle/API surface (pvmResume and VM pause/output types), directly related to the API gas-type signature updates.

🌐 Web query:

`AssemblyScript Map keys() iterator return type typed array`

💡 Result:

In AssemblyScript’s current standard library, `Map#keys()` does **not** return an iterator (and there’s no “typed array” iterator return type for it). It returns a **normal `Array<K>`** of the map’s keys (in insertion order) as a temporary/preliminary API “while iterators are not supported.” [1]

So the effective type is:

```ts
keys(): Array<K>
```

(Iterators for collection/typed-array methods like `keys()` are still tracked as not-yet-supported in the project roadmap.) [2]

**Sources:** [1] [2]

---

🌐 Web query:

`AssemblyScript unchecked() array access bounds checking`

💡 Result:

In AssemblyScript, `unchecked(expr)` tells the compiler to emit *unchecked operations* inside `expr`—notably including array/typed-array element loads/stores—so the usual index bounds check is skipped. Example from the official docs:

- `total += unchecked(arr[i])`
- `unchecked(arr[i] = value)` ([assemblyscript.org](https://www.assemblyscript.org/examples/arrays.html))

Important implications:

- This removes the *language-level* bounds check/exception path, but it does **not** make out-of-range accesses safe: WebAssembly will still **trap** with “memory access out of bounds” if the resulting address is outside linear memory. So you must guarantee indices are valid. ([surma.dev](https://surma.dev/things/js-to-asc/?utm_source=openai))
- You can control how `unchecked()` is applied globally with the compiler option `--uncheckedBehavior`:
  - `default`: unchecked ops only inside `unchecked()`
  - `never`: ignore `unchecked()`
  - `always`: use unchecked ops whenever possible ([assemblyscript.org](https://www.assemblyscript.org/compiler.html))

Citations:

- 1: https://www.assemblyscript.org/examples/arrays.html
- 2: https://surma.dev/things/js-to-asc/?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://www.assemblyscript.org/compiler.html

---

- **`Array<T>.length`** in AssemblyScript is a **mutable `i32` field**: `var length: i32` (you can also set it to grow/shrink the array). [1]

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`GitHub Actions pull_request event github.base_ref vs github.event.pull_request.base.sha difference documentation`

💡 Result:

- **`github.base_ref`** (Actions *context*) is the **name of the PR’s target branch** (the branch you’re merging *into*), e.g. `main`. It’s only set for `pull_request` / `pull_request_target`. [1]  
- **`github.event.pull_request.base.sha`** (the *webhook payload* field) is a **commit SHA associated with that base branch** in the pull request payload (i.e., a SHA, not a branch name). It is **not** the “merge-base” between the PR branch and the base branch; people frequently observe it as the base branch tip at PR creation time (and not necessarily what you expect for diffing). [2][3]

Related (often the source of confusion): for `pull_request` workflows, **`GITHUB_REF` is `refs/pull/<n>/merge` and `GITHUB_SHA` is the last merge commit on that merge ref**, not the base branch tip; GitHub explicitly notes to use `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` if you want the PR head commit. [4]

**Docs:**  
[1] GitHub Actions contexts (`github.base_ref`) — https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/accessing-contextual-information-about-workflow-runs  
[4] `pull_request` event semantics (`GITHUB_SHA`/`GITHUB_REF`, and `pull_request.head.sha`) — https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows  
**Discussion/behavior notes:**  
[2] “Unexpected value for `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`” (runner issue) — https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/1689  
[3] “The Many SHAs of a GitHub Pull Request” — https://www.kenmuse.com/blog/the-many-shas-of-a-github-pull-request/

---



</details>

**Use a fixed SHA instead of a branch name for baseline checkout.**

`${{ github.base_ref }}` is a branch name that points to the current HEAD of the base branch. If the base branch advances before this workflow runs, the baseline will be stale, making results non-reproducible.

Use `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` instead, which is a fixed commit SHA from the pull request payload (captured when the PR was created). This ensures the baseline remains constant across workflow runs.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       - name: Checkout base branch for baseline
         uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
-          ref: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
           path: ./baseline
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

